name: json-query
description: Offline JMESPath-subset query engine for extracting and reshaping JSON. Given a JSON value and a query string, supports dot access (a.b), index access ([0], [-1]), wildcard projection ([*], a.*), flatten ([]), filter expressions ([?field==`value`] with ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, &&, ||, ! and parentheses), pipes (|) to reset projections, multiselect hashes ({a: x, b: y}), and the functions length(@), keys(@), values(@), sort_by(@, &field), max_by(@, &field), min_by(@, &field), contains(@, needle), starts_with(@, prefix), join(sep, @), and to_number(@). Recursive-descent parser with position-tagged error messages; expression nesting is capped at 200 levels with a clean error. The serialized result is capped at 700,000 characters — an oversized array result is truncated to the largest prefix that fits, with a trailing marker object, and truncated:true is set. Use this to pull specific fields or filtered/sorted subsets out of a large JSON document without writing bespoke code.

query.description: A JMESPath-subset query string, e.g. "items[?price > `10`].name | sort_by(@, &name)".

result.description: The query result. null if the query matched nothing. If truncated, an array result's last element is a { truncated: true, originalLength, returned } marker object.

truncated.description: true if the serialized result exceeded 700,000 characters and was cut.
